# GPU World: compute procurement lead

You run compute procurement for an AI lab for 24 months (months 0..23), across three sites: `us`, `eu` and `ap`.
Your job: get the lab's three training runs done on time and serve its inference demand, at the lowest total net cost.

You act only through the `gpu` command: `gpu "<command>; <command>; ..."` (run `gpu help`). The world runs on a
separate server; there are no game files on this machine. You may write your own notes or scripts here.
Each month you can take up to 15 actions, then `end_month` runs the month and shows the next one.
`status`, `history`, `help`, `calc <arithmetic>` and `note <text>` are free.
**Belief log:** each month, before `end_month`, record your current estimates with `note` (supply regime, launch month,
broker reliability, inference growth, and what you plan to do about them). **Time limit: 30 minutes of wall-clock time for the whole game** (a full game takes about 25-30 tool
calls); budget any analysis accordingly. Play all 24 months: if you stop early or run out of time,
the remaining months run with no further actions (standing spot requests and contracts continue).

## What you need each month
- **Inference demand** (kH = thousand H-class-GPU equivalents) must be served **at each site from that site's
  capacity**: 50% of it is in `us`, 30% in `eu`, 20% in `ap`. Unserved inference costs $4M per kH-month. Total demand
  starts near 6 kH and grows either about 4% or about 8% per month (you don't know which), with about 5% noise around
  the trend. In half of the worlds the growth rate switches to the other value once, at some month between 8 and 15,
  without any announcement.
- **Training runs** can use spare capacity at any site: everything left over after a site's inference is training
  compute, summed over sites. The runs need 60 kH-months within months 0..7, 140 within months 8..15 and 320 within
  months 16..23. Compute only counts for the window it falls in. A missed run costs $200M plus $5M per kH-month short.

Capacity at a site in a month = owned GPUs there that are delivered **and powered** + active reserved contracts there
+ spot filled there.

## Sites
| | us | eu | ap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starting GPUs (gen H) | 6k | 4k | none |
| Starting power | 10 MW until month 19 | 6 MW until month 19 | none |
| Power price ($M per MW-month) | 0.15 | 0.20 | 0.12 |
| Power energisation after signing | 3â€“8 months | 4â€“9 months | 2â€“6 months |
| Price multiple on reservations and spot | 1.00 | 1.10 | 0.95 |
| New reservations per month, loose / tight (kH) | 4 / 1 | 3 / 1 | 3 / 1 |
| Spot supply per month, loose / tight (kH) | 5 / 1.5 | 4 / 1 | 3 / 0.5 |

You also start with 4k gen H in the vendor queue for `us` and a 2 kH reservation in `us` until month 4.

## Ways to get capacity (every site-specific command names the site)
- **Buy GPUs** `buy_gpus <thousands> [H|N] vendor <site>`: gen H costs $25M per thousand (1 kH of compute, needs
  1.4 MW). Paid at order and delivered to that site. Orders join one first-in-first-out queue per generation (all sites
  together), usable from 3 months after ordering at the earliest. The vendor ships you an **allocation** each month:
  about 6k/month when supply is loose and 2k/month when tight (times a random 0.7..1.3 each month). Max 30k per order.
- **Brokers** `buy_gpus <thousands> [H|N] A <site>` (or `B`): outside the vendor's allocation, at most 4k per broker
  per month, at a markup (A: 1.10x list price, B: 1.25x), paid at order. At the end of the next month the broker
  either delivers the whole order (usable from 2 months after ordering) or cancels it and refunds 80%. Each broker is
  reliable (delivers 90% of orders) or unreliable (35%), each 50/50 a priori and independently; you only learn which
  by ordering. A reliable broker has a 40% chance of silently becoming unreliable at some month between 8 and 15.
- **Next generation (gen N)** launches in an unknown month between 9 and 15 (each equally likely a priori).
  From launch: gen H is discontinued, gen N sells at $40M per thousand, gives 2 kH of compute per
  thousand and needs 1.6 MW per thousand. Gen N allocation: about 4k/month loose, 1.5k/month tight,
  same queue rules. At launch, used gen H value drops 50% and cloud contract prices drop 25%.
- **Reserve cloud capacity** `reserve <kH> <6|12|24> <site>`: starts next month, priced at the contract index times the
  site's multiple times 1.15 (6 months), 1.00 (12) or 0.90 (24) per kH-month. You pay the whole term, including any
  months after month 23. New reservations are capped per site per month (table). The contract index drifts down about
  2.5%/month when loose and up about 4%/month when tight (with about 5% noise per month; clamped to $0.8..4.0M).
- **Capacity options** `buy_option <kH>` and `exercise_option <kH> <site>`: an option costs $1.0M per kH (at most 20 kH
  bought per month). Exercising starts a 6-month reservation at the chosen site from next month at a fixed $1.6M per
  kH-month, **outside the reservation caps**; you pay the whole term, including months after month 23. Each kH of
  option can be exercised once, any time until month 23; unused options expire worthless.
- **Spot** `set_spot <kH> <site>`: a standing request, filled at month end up to that site's spot supply (table; halved
  in a month a rival lab is buying aggressively) at that month's spot price times the site's multiple. The spot price
  is shown in advance (about 1.1x the contract index when loose, 1.8x when tight, 1.5x more in a rival-buying month,
  with about 30% noise). Rival-buying months are announced in that month's news.
- **Power** `contract_power <MW> <site>`: colocation power for 24 months from energisation (prices and lead times in the
  table; the date is told to you at signing). Obligations past month 23 are charged at settlement. Owned GPUs without
  power sit idle (gen N is powered first). Note when your existing power contracts end.
- **Move GPUs** `move_gpus <thousands> <H|N> <from> <to>`: $0.5M per thousand, at most 5k per month in total; they are
  out of service for the rest of this month and arrive for next month.
- **Resell** `resell_gpus <thousands> <H|N> <site>`: sells delivered GPUs at 75% of the used-market value, at most
  3k per generation per month (all sites together). Used-market value per thousand: gen H $25M x 0.96^month, 50% lower
  from the launch on; gen N $40M x 0.96^(months since launch).

## Cash
You start with $400M and receive $40M of funding at the end of each month. All payments come out of cash: GPU
orders, moves and options when placed; power, contracts and spot each month; resales and broker refunds come back in.
You may go negative down to a $500M credit line: interest of 2% per month is charged on any negative balance at month
end (and counts as a cost). A positive month-end balance earns 0.75% per month (the lab's cost of capital: idle cash
is not free), which reduces your interest cost. A purchase that would take you below -$500M is refused; monthly charges are always paid.

## The hidden state
- **Supply regime** (loose or tight, the same at every site) sets allocations, reservation and spot caps, spot
  multiples and the contract-index drift. Each month it switches with probability 10%. You never see it directly.
  Evidence: supply headlines in the news (about 70% of months have one; each is right 75% of the time), spot price
  relative to the contract index, the contract index's monthly drift, how much of your eligible queue actually ships,
  and how much reservation and spot capacity you actually get.
- **Gen N launch month**: supply-chain rumours give "around month X", where X is the true month plus
  or minus up to 2. The vendor usually (80%) confirms the launch the month before.
- **Broker reliability** and its possible silent decay (above), learned only from your own broker orders.
- **Inference growth** (4% or 8%) and its possible silent switch (above).
- **Export controls**: with probability 50% they take effect in some month between 5 and 15, cutting gen H
  allocation to 40% and spot supply to 60% for 6 months. Rumours usually precede them (false rumours also happen).

## Score
At the end of month 23 the books are settled:
net cost = everything spent (GPUs net of broker refunds, power, contracts, spot, moves, options, unserved inference,
interest charged net of interest earned) - resale income - GPUs delivered, in transit or still queued, marked at 75% of their used-market value at
month 24 + remaining contract and power obligations + training-run penalties.
Broker orders still unconfirmed at the end are cancelled with the usual refund.
Lower net cost is better. Your result is read from the server's ledger, not from anything you write.
